subject: Jazz and Social Justice Performances
overview: The Medford Jazz Festival held its Saturday session at the West Medford Community Center, featuring performances by Receita de Samba and the Ally Project. The program integrated Brazilian musical traditions with jazz and spoken-word poetry focused on local history and social justice themes.

items.title: Festival Opening and Sponsor Acknowledgments
items.summary: Jonathan Fagan opened the session by recognizing festival volunteers and sponsors, including the Medford Arts Council and the West Medford Community Center.

items.title: Receita de Samba Musical Performance
items.summary: The ensemble Receita de Samba, featuring vocalist Ana Borges and pianist Bill Ward, performed a set of Brazilian bossa nova and samba compositions.

items.title: The Ally Project: Jazz and Social Justice
items.summary: Terry Carter and the Ally Project performed original compositions and spoken-word poetry exploring the history of the African-American community in West Medford, the impacts of gentrification, and broader themes of racial equity.

items.title: Sunday Schedule and Closing Remarks
items.summary: Organizers concluded the session with a preview of Sunday's lineup featuring students from the Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice and pianist George Russell Jr.
